answer: The pigment multiplier is published, charged in glacier, and copper lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 13 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 1115 identities would post 4574 proofs and burn roughly 61 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
